Here is the full CLI configuration to meet your requirements:

```cisco
configure terminal
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 description [WAN]-[CCT12345]-[100/1000]
 ip address 192.168.0.1 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown
 no ip proxy-arp
 no ip redirects
 no ip unreachables
 no ip mask-reply
 no cdp enable
 ip verify unicast source reachable-via rx allow default-route
 authentication mode enable
 authentication event fail action next-method
 authentication event success action log
 authentication logging billable
 authentication order dot1x mab
 service-policy input QoS-IN
end
write memory
```

**Configuration breakdown:**

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `configure terminal` | Enter global config mode |
| `interface GigabitEthernet0/1` | Enter interface config |
| `description [WAN]-[CCT12345]-[100/1000]` | Interface label per naming standard |
| `ip address 192.168.0.1 255.255.255.0` | Assign IP with /24 subnet |
| `no shutdown` | Administrative up (defaults to down) |
| `no ip proxy-arp` | Disables proxy ARP (security best practice) |
| `no ip redirects` | Prevents ICMP redirects (security) |
| `no ip unreachables` | Prevents ICMP unreachable messages |
| `no ip mask-reply` | Security - not responding to ICMP mask requests |
| `no cdp enable` | Disables CDP on this interface (info leak prevention) |
| `ip verify unicast source reachable-via rx allow default-route` | IP source guard (best practice for access/edge interfaces) |
| `authentication mode enable` | Configures 802.1X/MAB for authentication |
| `authentication event fail action next-method` | Allows MAB fallback on auth failure |
| `authentication event success action log` | Logs successful authentication |
| `authentication logging billable` | Enables AAA accounting |
| `authentication order dot1x mab` | Sets authentication order |
| `service-policy input QoS-IN` | Apply QoS policy (example name, adjust as needed) |
| `end` | Exit to privileged EXEC |
| `write memory` | Save configuration to NVRAM |
